event.name: Hernandez vs. Rodrigues
event.notes: "name" is matched as a substring against ESPN's own event name (punctuation and case are ignored, but spelling is NOT — no typo tolerance here, unlike fighter-name matching elsewhere in the pipeline), and the FIRST match in the scoreboard window wins. ESPN spells the main-event surname "Rodrigues" (Gregory Rodrigues, Brazilian) rather than the more common "Rodriguez" — confirm against ESPN before a run if this ever looks wrong. A one-off Fight Night is unique inside the 45-day lookahead so a short name like this is enough; for a weekly series (e.g. Contender Series) the name needs season+week instead, see git history. Discovery pulls recent uploads from each capper channel and keeps the ones whose title matches settings.discovery.title_contains. Add entries to "videos" only to pin a specific video by hand.

card.name: UFC Fight Night: Hernandez vs. Rodrigues

comments.comment: Believes Dyer ends up getting a finish.
Named as his free play of the week; Dyer has the power and technical striking edge while Reed is coming off a long layoff and has been finished inside the distance in most of her losses.

Reed has already been KO'd by Sajara Eubanks and is at the end of her career, and the UFC matched Dyer with a striker who won't take her down; they warned not to load up since it's roughly 50/50 between a KO and a decision.
Adam agreed it's an easy fight for Dyer and that this is likely the end of the road in the UFC for Reed, who he sees as a bottom-tier fighter.
A big favorite at plus money in what he believes is the most likely outcome; he didn't place it but likes it.
Reed leaves her head on the center line, has a bad chin and no fast-twitch athleticism, and has been finished by anyone with skill; Dyer should chin her in the first exchange.
Dyer is more talented and Reed's only real weapon is okay boxing; he doesn't see Reed out-striking or out-grappling her, expecting a first or second round TKO.
Reed is bottom-of-the-barrel competition and has been finished in every loss; Dyer should leg kick her, get her down and ground-and-pound a finish.

Both cappers land on Judice: she's the crisper, faster, higher-volume striker who doesn't slow down, and Jacob thinks Chavez is limited, will get worn down and possibly finished. Angelo notes the price is disgusting and he'd never bet it at 5-to-1, so it's a pick rather than a bet.
Named the lock of the night: better striker, volume, speed and movement, while Chavez barely beat a poor opponent in her debut.
Judice's output, speed and striking are far better, Chavez gets hit and dropped too much and shouldn't be able to get takedowns.
One of his most confident picks; Judice has proven herself against varied UFC-level opposition while Chavez hasn't faced good competition.
Leg of the three-pick parlay: Judice is a level above — quicker, more technical, more powerful striking — while Chavez comes forward recklessly and is very hittable.
Best bet as a parlay piece; he doesn't think Chavez is UFC level and Judice's boxing and combinations should pick her apart.
Judice's slick kickboxing, speed and range management are too much for the power-loading Chavez.
Judice is sharper, faster and improving each fight; her output and pace should be too much for the still-green Chavez.
Dyer is a big, strong, clean, technical striker facing someone who can be knocked out; he says he's very, very confident in Dyer and expects Reed to get finished.
Expects the fight to be more competitive than the -750 line since Reed is a good taekwondo specialist, but still sees Dyer getting the job done.
Dyer is the far better Muay Thai/kickboxing striker with power and speed, while Reed fights with her hands low, gets hit and has no quality wins.
Dyer is better everywhere and should outstrike Reed, who tends to get beaten up.
Listed as one of his most confident picks on the card; he believes Dyer beats Reed even on Reed's best day.
Dyer has the better, slicker kickboxing and range control while Reed is unimpressive on the feet and will be a step behind all fight.
Padilla's constant forward pressure, cage cutting and damage should beat the slowing Haqparast, who makes small striking defense mistakes.

Slam of the week: Padilla is better than Haqparast everywhere except pure boxing, and Haqparast is defensively porous (160 strikes absorbed vs Ribovics), coming off a brutal KO loss with lots of mileage.
Padilla is the smarter fighter with better grappling, elbows and round-stealing ability, while Haqparast gets hit far too much; good underdog value in a close fight.
Padilla's grimy pressure, clinch work and volume should grind out a 15-minute decision the way he did against Mederos.

People are sleeping on Padilla; his dirty pressure boxing, elbows, leg kicks and clinch work should win handily and he might even KO Haqparast, who is coming off a brutal knockout loss, and Padilla just dealt with a mover in his last fight.

Underdog lock of the card and an official money line play; he believes Padilla can apply heavy pressure and trade damaging shots like Rivovic and Jared Gordon did to Haqparast, winning by decision or late TKO.

Haqparast's recent wins were close/split decisions he could have lost and he gets hit a lot, while Padilla is durable, high-volume with nasty elbows, knees and kicks and good cardio for three rounds; sees him winning by decision or TKO.
Brody rides with Taco's fight IQ and game-plan discipline and won't bet on Haqparast coming off a brutal KO layoff.

picks.selection: Anthony Wint by KO in round 1

comments.comment: Wint just won on Contender Series taking no damage and has quick KO power; Chapman shies away when punches come at him.
Tailor-made matchup for Wint's athleticism and power; Chapman lacks the size and physicality to clinch and wear him down.
The former linebacker will charge through Chapman, push him to the fence and ground-and-pound; they see no world where this reaches round two.
He expects Wint to blitz Chapman and get another quick first round finish.
Jacob says Schultz has forgotten how to shoot takedowns and has non-existent striking, while McVey has flashes of belonging with knees, elbows and offensive wrestling.
Schultz has abysmal striking and atrocious takedowns and immediately sits to his back; McVey is bigger with much better striking.
Lean toward McVey because he uses his kickboxing and range better in what should be a striking fight.
Official prediction: McVey is a ferocious clinch fighter with a string of round-one finishes and he expects him to rough Schultz up early, though he's still waiting on props.
McVey has a higher ceiling, is more explosive on the feet, has submission and clinch/cage work, and is the slight favorite; leaning to a second-round TKO.
Leg in his long shot prelim parlay.
Leg of the +110 two-leg parlay; McVey has improved a lot since the amateur loss years ago, should stop Schultz's takedowns, win the clinch with knees and elbows, and possibly finish him.

Schultz has atrocious takedown defense, poor striking and cardio, and was controlled by a retired 35-year-old kickboxer; McVey should beat him up in the clinch and get him out early, though not a fight to lay big units on.

picks.fight: Reinier de Ridder vs Roman Dolidze

comments.comment: De Ridder is the better striker of two poor strikers and the better grappler, plus he's no longer draining himself to make middleweight; included in the 'basic' picks.
Thinks the odds are far too wide and wouldn't bet much, but de Ridder's superior grappling and control time should sneak him a close, possibly decision win.
De Ridder is huge at light heavyweight after too many weight cuts, and should bully Dolidze with size and knees up the middle; very confident he wins even if there's no finish.
De Ridder is the longer, more varied striker, better in the clinch and can get takedowns; Dolidze is older with cardio issues. Leans toward a decision.
Best bet and a parlay piece; de Ridder is bigger, longer, better on the feet, in cardio, wrestling and jiu-jitsu, and Dolidze struggles off his back.
Wint's athleticism, method and power should find the big shot for a first-round knockout, though Chapman may be more competitive than expected.
Wint is an athletic heavyweight prospect and the fight is set up for Chapman to get knocked out; a Chapman win would be one of the biggest upsets of the year.
Wint is poised when striking as shown on Contender Series, can take Chapman down or land a big shot, and looks set up for an easy matchup.
He calls -145 unbelievable odds for a former NFL linebacker who hits like a freight train against a small, non-athletic opponent.
Wint is an explosive, athletic heavyweight with all finishes while Chapman is out of shape with poor competition; he'll land and Chapman goes down (though the -1000 price is too big).
Wint has crazy power and athleticism while Chapman is out of shape with a padded record; a layup debut finish.
Jones's pace, pressure and chaos plus his grappling should break Mederos down in rounds two and three and win on the scorecards.
Jones is durable, bigger, has dog in him and makes opponents fight a dirty fight, while Mederos moves backwards constantly and doesn't sit down on shots.
Jones is more well-rounded with better activity and can mix in wrestling, while Mederos can go passive; sees Jones pulling away after an early competitive round.
Prediction is Jones by decision; he's skilled everywhere, ferocious, and should duplicate the success Chris Padilla had against Mederos - he even says he may have talked himself into the moneyline.
Mederos is technically better but Jones's relentless pressure, durability and volume make it the ugly, bloody fight Mederos doesn't want.
Leg of a +110 two-leg parlay; Jones's constant pressure and cage-cutting will wear down an opponent who wants to fight at range, leading to a late finish or decision.
Mederos can be paced and grappled; Jones' relentless pressure, output and better grappling should take over the later rounds, likely a Jones decision, though the line may be a bit wide.
Douglas is the new boogeyman in the UFC and should walk Emmers down and shrug off his takedowns.
Douglas is a well-rounded, powerful prospect with good striking and takedowns, but he expects a competitive fight rather than the blowout the public predicts.
Douglas has knockout power that lower-level guys like Emmers can't handle; he was dropping Orosa with jabs.
Douglas is quick, covers ground, occupies with the jab and comes over the top; they think he clips Emmers, and the moneyline price is fine for the juicer parlay.
Douglas has heavy hands, a good high guard and strong boxing; sees value at -390 and used him as a parlay leg.
Prediction is Douglas by round-one knockout given seven straight knockout wins and deceptive lunging power, though he hasn't yet committed a bet.
Leg of the three-pick parlay: Douglas has power, has been leveling up fight to fight and just beat a crafty opponent, while Emmers is aging and his two wins are nothing to hang your hat on.
Calls it an easy pick: Douglas is a powerhouse with strong calf kicks and Emmers is outmatched.
Expects Douglas to walk Emmers down and eventually find a big knockout.
Douglas is dangerous enough on the feet that Emmers eventually can't take wrestling entry risks without getting caught.
Best bet; he won't pay -390 on the moneyline, and believes Emmers only wins if it goes to decision, so if Douglas wins it's by knockout after stuffing takedowns.
Adam sees it as a showcase fight and expects Douglas to knock Emmers out in the first round.
Believes Emmers will engage in boxing but be a step behind and won't take Douglas's straight punches.
Emmers is 37, was chinned by Nate Landwehr and boxed up by Jack Jenkins; Douglas has six straight knockouts and crazy power, though there's some worry about Emmers' takedowns.
Douglas's jab and KO power plus his move to a better gym; thinks he hurts Emmers early and finishes against the cage, though he admits there is value on Emmers.
Expects Douglas to establish low kicks then crack Emmers upstairs for an early first-or-second-round finish.

Sam was shocked Nzechukwu was an underdog: Gaziev looks fatter, is nearly 37 and took heavy damage in his last fights, while Nzechukwu is now coaching basics and just needs a jab and leg kick plus a wrestling edge.
Lesser of two evils pick: Nzechukwu is quicker, more athletic with better stance and striking, and Gaziev fights with low hands, gasses and quit on the stool.
Calls it a 50/50 and says he isn't confident enough to parlay it, but Nzechukwu picks his shots and has looked better at heavyweight if Gaziev strikes with him.

Gaziev has been knocked out three times and won't wrestle much, so Nzechukwu only has to manage striking range where he has knockout power; also good takedown defense after a full camp for a grappler.
His 'plus money dog' — Gaziev's gas tank is poor and he's sloppy on the feet, while Nzechukwu is more technical with decent takedown defense and should take over late.
Gaziev struggled badly against Rozenstruik when he couldn't get the fight to the mat, and Nzechukwu is durable, hard to take down and can piece him up from the outside with length and power.
Wint should smoke his overmatched opponent in a few minutes; parlayed with the Spivak/Petrino over 1.5.
Leg of the two-fight under parlay: Wint is a physical specimen with the death touch coming off multiple sub-60-second knockouts, while Chapman is slow and out of shape.
Both fighters are very tough so he expects the fight to go past 2.5.
Haqparast is hard to finish and Padilla lacks the power, so this should go the distance.
Both men are very tough so he expects the fight to go long.
He bet the over because he thinks this one is a grind that goes the distance.
If Gaziev wins it has to be in round one, so they take the under and hope for violence either way.
Both big men will swing early; if it gets past round two it probably goes to decision.
Wint is a -950 favorite against a guy who doesn't belong in the UFC; used as a parlay and round robin anchor.
Calls it a setup fight for Wint, whose athleticism, poise and ground-and-pound should win easily; happy to parlay him.
Wint just demolished Matt Adams on Contender Series and Chapman is a low-output, unimpressive striker.
Massive gap in competition — Barbosa knocked out his debut opponent and ran the LFA gauntlet while Kuse fought cans; expects an early knockout.
Says third-round TKO or decision, but leans more toward Judice winning clearly on volume.
Expects Judice to attack with head kicks and jabs and dominate, but thinks Chavez is very durable and won't be finished despite everyone being on the KO.
Value play at plus money since he leans toward Judice winning a decision after picking Chavez apart.
Adam thinks Judice is one of the most exciting women's fighters and doesn't rate Chavez, but expects a point fight to go the distance.
Judice is rangy, technical with good takedown defense and has faced better competition; expects her to win a striking battle on the scorecards.
Official call is Judice winning wide on the cards (30-26/30-27) because Chavez is tough and takes a beating.
He sees Judice picking Chavez apart from distance for 15 minutes and winning on the cards.

picks.fight: Reinier de Ridder vs Roman Dolidze
picks.selection: Reinier de Ridder inside the distance

comments.comment: De Ridder looks rejuvenated at 205 with devastating knees up the middle that could lead to a KO or a submission on a hurt Dolidze.
He thinks Spivak can win outright but bought points for protection; Petrino is athletic but a quitter and struggles defensively in grappling.

picks.selection: Marcio Barbosa in round 1 by KO

comments.comment: Barbosa has huge knockout power and almost all of his wins come in round one, though Kuse is live if he can extend the fight since Barbosa fades.

picks.selection: Vitor Petrino by KO in round 1

comments.comment: Expects Petrino to land heavy early and Spivac to crumble; 'down to hit that' at the price.

picks.selection: Kennedy Nzechukwu to win inside the distance in round 1

comments.comment: Nzechukwu can knock out any heavyweight if he lands clean and Gaziev will be there to be hit, though Adam is unsure about his aggression.
Expects an action-packed first round where either guy could win by submission or KO.
Suggested parlaying this fight's under 2.5 with the other unders on the card since they expect a finish.
Believes whoever wins this fight wins by decision, so the distance prop is a good spot.
Preferred way to play it since Colby doesn't like picking Haqparast outright but expects the fight to go to the scorecards.
He bet the point spread expecting a tight, grinding fight that Jones wins without dominance.

picks.selection: Jackson McVey to finish in round 1

comments.comment: All seven of McVey's wins come in the first round (KO or submission off a takedown attempt), and they dismiss Schultz's win over a retired, out-of-shape Ben Johnston.
Says he has almost no confidence but has to make a prediction; sees a quick one-round fight where McVey catches Schultz coming in.
They don't see the fight getting past round two; if it does they'd live bet Schultz because McVey would be gassing.

picks.selection: Le'Veon Douglas by KO in round 1 or 2

comments.comment: Calls Douglas the hardest hitting featherweight on the roster and believes he's fixed his issues with pressure; warns Emmers' pressure and takedowns are the risk.
Douglas is on a six-fight KO streak out of Cub Swanson's gym and blew out Julian Erosa, who they rate above the 37-year-old Emmers; it's in their parlay.

picks.fight: Reinier de Ridder vs Roman Dolidze
picks.selection: Reinier de Ridder by submission in round 2 or 3

comments.comment: Floated as an interesting angle given RDR's grappling edge, though they question whether Dolidze ever gets submitted.
Rodrigues' danger factor and power are too much, Hernandez should struggle to get takedowns; prefers the moneyline over the +200 KO prop in case of a submission or decision.
Rodriguez has power, precision and world-class grappling with improved cardio, and Hernandez is weak to the body and can be hurt; they expect Robocop to do damage in the first three rounds.
Rodrigues is massive and powerful, Hernandez's takedown entries are poor and he's soft to the body; nearly calls it an underdog lock and uses it as a parlay leg.

Hernandez has never faced anyone like Rodrigues; takedowns will be very hard against a really good wrestler/grappler, and Rodrigues hits harder than anyone Hernandez has faced and can hurt him on the feet.
Called his 'savage underdog lock' — Rodrigues hits like a truck and he doesn't see Hernandez surviving that power or easily getting takedowns, expecting a first or second round finish.
PrizePicks play; both are talented and Spivac can weather an early storm and use wrestling to slow Petrino down, elongating the fight.
Neither man is an insane first-round finisher and both are tough, so the fight should go longer; parlayed with the Wint under 1.5 at -104.
Petrino gasses and Spivac has the IQ to change levels, wrestle and take the later rounds.
Jacob says he played Spivac: his jab is elite and will frustrate and eat up Petrino, and Jacob thinks Spivac is the better striker and better wrestler, with Petrino only relying on athleticism.
Admits he has no read and says don't take his opinion, but favors Spivac as more well-rounded with better proven conditioning and grappling.
They think Petrino is overrated and Spivac wins a crafty 29-28; the moneyline is an alternative to the decision prop.

Spivak is criminally underrated with a strong jab, arguably beat Waldo, and is clearly the better grappler and bigger man; Petrino only wins by finding one big shot and has been dropped and submitted before.
Petrino is flaky and untrustworthy (losses to Anthony Smith and Jacoby, nearly finished by Aslund), while Spivak has far more heavyweight experience, strong wrestling and improved striking.
Spivak's sharp straight punches, underrated chin and strong grappling make him roughly a 60% favorite in his eyes, yet he's priced as the dog; likes a TKO/ground-and-pound or submission finish.
Jones' ability to create wars and force pocket exchanges, plus leaning on his grappling, should grind out a decision over the athletic Medeiros.
Adam thinks Mason Jones is underrated and really good, and expects a back-and-forth fight that Jones wins on the cards.
Mederos lacks the power to hurt Jones, and once Jones realizes that he'll start styling; not confident in a finish so take the decision.
Petrino's heavyweight power is the difference; if Spivak can't consistently get him down he'll have problems standing in front of him.
Petrino looks better at heavyweight without the weight cut, has power and a good ground game, while Spivak has a bad chin.
Petrino hits far too hard for Spivak's jab-based game and heavyweights don't get up well off their back; only risk is Petrino needlessly wrestling into a guillotine.
He expects Petrino to unload a big combination and put Spivac out, calling a second round KO.
McVey has grown since their amateur meeting, is much stronger and more well-rounded; he should keep it standing with defensive grappling and batter Schultz with knees and elbows in the clinch.
Best bet for the fight; McVey is the bigger, better striker and Schultz gasses after about three minutes, so he doesn't want to pay -172 when he expects a finish.
McVey is bigger, nasty in the clinch with elbows, and Schultz has a bad chin and doesn't like being hit.
He sees McVey landing a knee or elbow from the clinch to put Schultz down.

picks.selection: Gregory Rodrigues by KO in round 1 or 2

comments.comment: Calls it a free bet with flipped odds: Rodrigues is powerful and durable while Hernandez is 'pillow handed' and can't finish him early, so the bet either wins or voids.
Hernandez chose to box Strickland and shot no takedowns, and Rodrigues hits harder with two rounds of cardio; if it reaches round three Hernandez takes over.
A hedge play on the main event since an early KO is the most likely scenario if Rodrigues wins.
Adam officially switched his pick to Dorsainvil because of Young's cut and because Dorsainvil's win over Dan Hooker-level opponent (Dan Halt) is the best win between the two.
Named his underdog of the night and best bet: Dorsainvil's forward pressure, heavy shots and wrestling should win the scorecards against a Young who wants to move and use range.
They think Dyer wins inside the distance and suggested parlaying this fight's under 2.5 with other unders on the card.
He expects Dyer to beat Reed up badly and get a finish.
The only bet he has placed on this fight; he thinks whether McVey wins or loses it likely ends inside a round and a half.

All of McVey's fights and most of Schultz's have ended under 1.5 rounds; both have big finishing upside early — McVey with KOs and front chokes, Schultz with quick submissions — so he takes the under rather than a side.
Expect an early finish; the under price is close to McVey's moneyline.

picks.fight: Reinier de Ridder vs Roman Dolidze

comments.comment: De Ridder's grappling is too much for Dolidze's stalking slugger style; he should wrap him up, take him down and find a submission.
The move to 205 gives a bigger, fresher version of himself which should make his chain wrestling and submission grappling even more effective.
Value play and cycle parlay leg; expects de Ridder to take Dolidze down and submit him in the second round once Dolidze tires.
Young has a full camp and prior UFC experience, and his decision loss to Colon looks fine in hindsight, while Dorseinvil debuts on short notice.
Young has 14 pro fights versus Dosainvil's six, and Young's volume should add up against Dosainvil's poor defense; expects a close decision.
Young is tough with great cardio, proven against better competition, and Dorsainvil is on short notice; expects a 29-28 decision.

picks.selection: Carli Judice to win, over 1.5 rounds

comments.comment: Leg of the +103 two-leg parlay; Judice is the far superior kickboxer with better range management and should pick Chavez apart to a decision rather than an early finish.
Rodriguez hits like a freight train with fight-ending body kicks and huge power, and Hernandez is breakable (KO'd by Kevin Holland, hurt by Michel Pereira, possible rib issue).
Expects Rodrigues to stuff takedowns, keep it standing and hurt the hittable Hernandez to the body or with heavy hands.

Rodrigues is bigger, more physical and more powerful with elite BJJ and thudding body kicks; Hernandez has no knockout power, has been hurt to the body by everyone, and abandoned his takedown-heavy game plan against Strickland.
Rodrigues has the size, power and underrated grappling to avoid being dominated, and Hernandez is vulnerable to body work; expects a TKO in the first two rounds.
He doesn't see the fight reaching round three and predicts Rodrigues touches Hernandez's chin for a second round knockout.

picks.selection: Fight does not start the 5th round

comments.comment: Hernandez pushes a crazy pace and Rodrigues is a power puncher, so he expects a finish either way in a high-action fight before the fifth round.

picks.selection: Chanel Dyer by KO in round 2

comments.comment: Dyer is the bigger, more powerful striker with a kickboxing/Muay Thai base and good volume; he expects her to catch Reed, likely to the body, like she did against Ravena Oliveira.
He expects Dyer to pick Reed apart and eventually land a finishing shot, calling it a second round finish.

picks.selection: Anthony Wint to win in under 0.5 rounds

comments.comment: He scored a 34-second KO on Contender Series and Chapman has nothing for him, so the plus-money half-round line is live.

picks.selection: Leon Douglas to win and under 1.5 rounds (same game)

comments.comment: Douglas is the hardest hitter at 145, Emmers is 37 and hasn't used his grappling, and the straight KO (-200) and moneyline (-400) prices are unplayable so they take the same-game price.

picks.selection: Carli Judice by KO or decision

comments.comment: Safer way to back Judice since a submission is the unlikely outcome.
Sees Haqparast as the better boxer by a wide margin with good takedown/clinch defense, and thinks Padilla is too small to physically wear him down.
Haqparast's volume and pace should edge close rounds and Padilla lacks the finishing ability to put him away; expects 29-28.
Colby thinks Haqparast is bigger and better on the feet and doesn't believe Padilla can take him down, but won't play it heavy.

picks.selection: Chris Padilla to win in round 2

comments.comment: Adam takes round 2 because the stats support a Padilla round-two victory; both agree it won't be round one.
Doesn't have a great read but thinks Gaziev has looked horrendous in his last two fights, so he takes Nzechukwu by knockout in round two or three.
Gaziev gasses and gets dropped by jabs; Kennedy knows how to get off the fence and should catch him with a straight.
Doesn't believe in Gaziev's chain wrestling and thinks Nzechukwu is elusive enough to low kick and clip the 'blob'; second or third round TKO.

picks.selection: Kennedy Nzechukwu by KO in round 1

comments.comment: Good price on an early knockout since Gaziev swings wild and gets clipped early.

picks.selection: Gregory Rodriguez to win in under 3.5 rounds

comments.comment: That's the only way Rodriguez wins, and it covers multiple rounds and both finish methods (KO or choke/ground and pound).
